name: Rich Text Content
summary: Rich text content is writing somebody else wrote — from a CMS, an editor, a Markdown file — rendered inside a box of your own. Use it wherever you cannot add a class to the markup, because the styling has to hang off the elements instead. Whatever structure did not survive the trip is simply gone, and a box that scrolls is also a control.
demoNote: Every readout here is written by hand and checked against the real accessibility tree by the spec, so it cannot drift. Everything under Common mistakes is live, and each failing surface sits beside a correct one that looks the same.

contract.useWhen: A scrolling box of prose, named from the heading inside it.
keyboard: the surface is a stop, and an inner scroller is a second one
failureModes: overflow-x and nothing else, so Chromium gives it a stop with no role and no name
all three attributes kept once the surface no longer scrolls — a landmark that does nothing
overflow:hidden with a fade, which gets no tab stop at all and cannot be scrolled
the attribution inside the blockquote rather than in a figcaption beside it
heading rules that leave letter-spacing and text-transform open, so the host page cascades in
a positive outline-offset on the inner ring, which the surface clips
